subject: Nighthawk variant onboarding — provisional pin + compat sync
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@nettlelabs.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:04:00Z
Subject: Nighthawk variant onboarding — provisional pin + compat sync

Hi team,

Nettle Labs (cc'd) handed us a fresh variant: Nighthawk-3B-composite. They want to go live with it in a staged rollout next month, but have asked for a provisional pin on the Redwood side until we finish compatibility validation.

Attachments: nighthawk-3b-specs.pdf, nighthawk-compat-matrix.csv

Ask: can we get a short risk assessment and a recommendation for a provisional pin (duration + rollback triggers)? Key product asks from Nettle:
- No behavioral regressions on standard chat prompts (low tolerance)
- Preserve current latency SLOs for their tier (p95 <= 220ms token time)
- Tokenizer parity with Nighthawk-v1 (they flagged some prompt truncation in early tests)

Timeline: they want a go/no-go by 2026-05-24 so they can align release windows.

Marissa — can you lead the customer coordination (release window, canary cohort)?
Laura & Dev — can you evaluate tokenization/kv-compat + perf risks and propose whether a provisional pin is warranted?
Priyom — please add any telemetry or eval prompts we should run (preferably <500 prompts) that would highlight regressions.

CC'd Nettle Ops for visibility — feel free to add any detail about your acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: nighthawk-3b-specs.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: nighthawk-compat-matrix.csv (text/csv)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops@nettlelabs.com
Date: 2026-05-18T13:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Nighthawk variant onboarding — provisional pin + compat sync

Thanks Jasmine — quick read-through notes and open questions:

1) Tokenizer: the spec indicates they switched to a bpe variant with a slightly different merge table. That explains the truncation reports. We need a sample tokenizer file to run parity checks (byte offsets and decode/encode roundtrip).

2) KV / cache: the composite variant increases per-token KV state by ~8% according to their spec. That may change our batching thresholds and GPU memory pins. We should run a small memory-pressure test on staging.

3) Quantization profile: they recommend int8-ptq. Priyom, if you can run our 200 prompt eval with both int8 and fp16, call out any quality deltas.

Provisional pin recommendation (initial thought): allow provisional pin for 14 days with the following rollback triggers: 
- any >3% drop in Rouge/semantic-similarity on the eval set OR
- sustained p95 token latency degradation >15% for two consecutive 1-hr windows OR
- tokenizer mismatch causing >1% prompt corruption errors reported by customer.

I can take the owner role for the compatibility checklist; Dev, can you scope the smoke tests and estimate time? If we can get a quick tokenizer file from Nettle, I can run parity checks by EOD tomorrow.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Infra & Serving Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops@nettlelabs.com
Date: 2026-05-19T08:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Nighthawk variant onboarding — provisional pin + compat sync

Quick update after an initial smoke run on staging (see attached smoke-test-logs.txt):

- Tokenizer: we attempted an encode/decode roundtrip with the provided sample weights bundle yesterday afternoon. There is a deterministic offset for a subset of tokens (characters near emoji ranges and code-snippets) — that aligns with Nettle's truncation notes.

- Memory: the KV increase is real but within the margin if we adjust continuous-batch-size down by 8-10%. That preserves p95 in our short-run but we'll want to validate at scale.

- Perf: on small batches (<8 concurrent requests) p95 is within SLO. At higher concurrency we see tail spikes tied to cache thrashing; mitigations: temporary batching cap + prefix caching TTL increase.

Recommendation: provisional pin for 10 business days (rather than 14) to shorten exposure and expedite rollback if needed — with an automatic fallback to Nighthawk-v1 after 10 business days unless an approved extension is logged.

I'll attach logs and a short runbook for temporary batching caps.

[Attachment: smoke-test-logs.txt (text/plain)]

-dev

From: ops@nettlelabs.com <ops@nettlelabs.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-19T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Nighthawk variant onboarding — provisional pin + compat sync

Thanks team — appreciate the quick runs and recommendations. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tokenizer file: attaching the tokenizer_v3b.json here (we've also uploaded to your Drive link). We saw truncation primarily in messages with embedded markdown/code blocks.
- Latency: our internal perf window is tight; we need p95 <= 220ms token time. We can accept a provisional pin for 10 business days as long as we have a named owner and a rollback plan in case the latency threshold is hit.

Acceptance criteria for the provisional:
1) Tokenizer parity checks completed with <0.5% decode errors on the eval prompts.
2) Telemetry hooks enabled to surface prompt corruption events in the first 48 hours.
3) A canary cohort limited to 3% of production traffic for the first 72 hours.

We're available for a quick call tomorrow morning to finalize the canary cohort and handoff details.

— Priya N. (Nettle Ops)
[Attachment: tokenizer_v3b.json (application/json)]
